description: Rules that say when a save, or the running game, holds a state our mods should never be in (docs/development/test-automation.md). Save checks: python scripts/query-save.py checks. Live checks, which take a snapshot of the running game (ask the owner first): python scripts/perf.py look-check. How a check is written: external/phobos-modkit/docs/checks.md. A rule's note (kit 1.129.0) gives figures for the test list, read by test-pass from the newest saves and judged by config/test-evidence.json. A finding is not an in-game test, and a rule can be wrong.

checks.title: Vehicles saved no NaN or infinity in our values
checks.why: A NaN or infinity is the mark of a division by nothing; once saved it spreads through every figure worked out from it.

checks.title: Vehicles refer only to things the save holds
checks.why: The game drops a reference to a thing it cannot find when it loads, with an error: a hitch, a winch or a crew job left pointing at nothing.

checks.title: A vehicle's battery charge, coolant and oil stay between empty and full
checks.fault: min([charge, coolant, oil]) < 0 or max([charge, coolant, oil]) > 1.0001
checks.why: Each is a share of full (Framework's vehicle systems); outside 0 to 1 a rule has added or taken past its end. The 0.0001 allows for rounding.

checks.title: No vehicle part's health is below nothing
A vehicle's event log keeps no more than its 64 events
checks.why: VehicleEventLog.MaxCount is 64; more means its trimming stopped working and the save will keep growing.

checks.title: A vehicle's logbook keeps no more than its 200 entries
checks.why: LogbookRule.DefaultCap is 200; more means its trimming stopped working.

checks.title: A work store holds far more than any order of fittings takes
checks.says: {sum(stacks)} things laid out ({unique(kinds)}) for {count(orders)} fit orders
checks.why: Since Framework 0.286.2 the store keeps only what the waiting work needs. 300 is an authored line: about the most steel a heavy truck's dearest fittings take together.

checks.title: A work store holds no more than its waiting work could use
checks.says: {vehicle}{number}: {sum(held)} laid out, its waiting repairs and fittings could use {sum(needs)}
checks.why: Reads every option of every waiting repair, so it allows more than the store keeps. Due services' supplies are not read: 100 is an authored allowance for them.

checks.title: No destroyed vehicle's systems are still held in memory
checks.why: A snapshot includes garbage the collector has not reclaimed yet: a finding here is a leak only if python scripts/perf.py look-why Phobos.VehicleSystems.CompPhobosVehicleSystems finds something still holding it.

checks.title: A generator set's service lead takes its 300 W
checks.why: Figures for row 58, read live (kit 1.134.0: a snapshot is not kept, so the kit keeps the note). leadWatts is derived on the generator set's rare tick and never saved, so only the running game holds it: serviceLeadWatts 300 (Rules_VehicleSystems.xml), less only when the set offers less (GeneratorRule.StepWithLead). Read while a lead is run to a truck (leadTo set). Only the player runs a service lead, so no ofPlayer: a live check cannot tell yet.

checks.title: Each jet's guns are its own mod's copy of the fixed-wing code
checks.fault: (jet == "Harrier_Jet" and (contains(guns, "CloseAirSupport.Flight.VtolVehicleTurret") or contains(guns, "EA6BProwler.Flight.VtolVehicleTurret"))) or ((jet == "Warthog_Jet" or jet == "Frogfoot_Jet") and (contains(guns, "AV8BHarrier.Flight.VtolVehicleTurret") or contains(guns, "EA6BProwler.Flight.VtolVehicleTurret"))) or (jet == "Prowler_Jet" and (contains(guns, "AV8BHarrier.Flight.VtolVehicleTurret") or contains(guns, "CloseAirSupport.Flight.VtolVehicleTurret")))
checks.says: a {jet} saved with another jet mod's guns: {unique(guns)}
checks.why: Since 26 Nov 2026 the Harrier, Close Air Support and the Prowler each carry their own copy of the flight code. A jet saved under another mod's copy runs that code without its own fixed-wing data: no Sortie, a hover for a take-off (Patches 0.45.2 puts it right on load). A check cannot read a thing's own class, so this reads its guns, saved with it.

checks.title: A graded Cherokee chemtank's health follows its grade, through a save
checks.why: Figures for row 9 (test automation round two, 26 Nov 2026). A grade's healthFactor (PartGrades.xml: heavy-duty 1.3, salvaged 0.7) raises or lowers a part's maximum, and a load puts it back before health is restored, so a saved health above 120 can only be the raised maximum kept through a save; nothing can go above 156. 120 is the Chemtank's health in Vanilla Vehicles Expanded's Cherokee, and li[19] its place among the Cherokee's parts, both as of 26 Nov 2026: Vehicle Framework saves its own parts by place, not name, so a VVE update that reorders them makes this read another part. Only a Cherokee with one graded part is read, so the grade read is the chemtank's.

checks.title: A Cherokee's ferry tank holds three quarters again, and no more
checks.says: fuel {fuel}, above the 735 a stock tank and a ferry tank hold
checks.why: Figures for row 67 (test automation round two). The ferry tank's fuelCapacityFactor is 1.75 (Fittings.xml), so fuel above the stock tank's 420 (Vanilla Vehicles Expanded's Cherokee) shows the larger capacity in force, and above 735 is the capacity that keeps growing after a save and load, which the row watches for.

checks.title: A Harrier's ferry tank holds three quarters again, and no more
checks.says: fuel {fuel}, above the 437.5 a stock tank and a ferry tank hold
checks.why: As for the Cherokee: the Harrier's stock tank is 250. The Harrier saves its own vehicle class, so it is chosen by its def: a class select of Vehicles.VehiclePawn never reaches it.

checks.title: Heavy controls halve an aircraft's flight control, or cut it to 0.7 with manual reversion
checks.when: ofPlayer and count(samples(hydraulics, 0, 1)) >= 10 and last(samples(hydraulics, 0, 1)) < 0.4 and max(samples(hydraulics, 0, 1)) >= 0.7

note.variant: {'manual reversion' if kind == 'Warthog_Jet' or kind == 'Frogfoot_Jet' else 'powered'}
note.detail: flight control {round(last(samples(control, 0, 1)), 3)} of its day's best {round(max(samples(control, 0, 1)), 3)}, hydraulics {round(last(samples(hydraulics, 0, 1)), 3)}

checks.why: Figures for row 101, from the saved graph histories (kit 1.130.0; test automation round two). Below 0.4 flight hydraulics the controls are heavy and FlightControl is multiplied by 0.5, or by 0.7 where the loadout has manual reversion (Systems_Avionics.xml; the A-10's and Su-25's loadouts). Read only when the hydraulics were sound (0.7 or more) earlier in the saved day, so the day's best flight control is the sound one; a part damaged in between muddies the share. flightControl is derived, so only its history holds it. Ranges 0..1 from Systems_FlightControls.xml and Systems_Avionics.xml.

checks.title: A camped vehicle's night heater keeps its coolant warm
checks.when: ofPlayer and heater == True and pack == None and count(samples(coolant, -60, 200)) >= 40
checks.why: Figures for row 27, from the saved graph histories (kit 1.130.0). The night heater runs only at a caravan's camp (or for a bunk sleeper), pulling the coolant toward engineHeaterTarget 40 C, full below 35 (Systems_Cooling.xml), where a truck camped without it sits at the air's temperature. A vehicle in a caravan is a world object in the save, and only the player switches loads, so a world-object vehicle with its night heater on is the player's caravan. Read the save made at camp: a caravan on the move runs its engine hot. Range -60..200 from Systems_Cooling.xml.

checks.title: An electric vehicle's night heater costs about a fifth of its charge over ten hours, and holds the pack near 15 C
checks.when: ofPlayer and heater == True and pack != None and count(samples(charge, 0, 1)) >= 100 and max(diffs(tail(samples(charge, 0, 1), 100))) <= 0.0005
checks.why: Figures for row 71, from the saved graph histories (kit 1.130.0). nightHeaterShare is 0.02 of the charge an hour, about a fifth over ten hours, and nightHeaterPackTarget 15 C (Systems_Electric.xml). Read only when the charge never rose over the last ten hours (no charging in between) and the vehicle is a world object with its night heater on: the player's caravan. Ranges: charge 0..1 (Systems_Electrical.xml), pack -60..200 (Systems_Electric.xml).

checks.title: A worn engine burns oil faster, twice as fast at 40% health
checks.when: ofPlayer and count(samples(oil, 0, 1)) >= 11 and count(samples(load, 0, 1)) >= 10 and count(samples(engine, 0, 1)) >= 1 and sum(tail(samples(load, 0, 1), 10)) >= 3 and max(diffs(tail(samples(oil, 0, 1), 11))) <= 0.0001 and first(tail(samples(oil, 0, 1), 11)) - last(samples(oil, 0, 1)) <= 0.0035

note.variant: {'worn' if last(samples(engine, 0, 1)) <= 0.42 else 'sound' if last(samples(engine, 0, 1)) >= 0.98 else 'part worn'}

checks.why: Figures for row 28, from the saved graph histories (engineLoad's and engineCondition's kept since Framework 0.346.0, the owner's yes of 27 Nov 2026). The oil burns oilBurnPerHour 0.0015 times the engine's load times the engine's wear curve, 2 at 40% health to 1 when sound (Systems_Lubrication.xml, burn), so the last hour's oil lost over 0.00015 times the sum of its ten load samples is that curve: about 2 worn, 1 sound. Read only over an hour with no oil added (no sample rises), a real load (mean 0.3 or more), and no more lost than a worn engine at full load can burn (0.0035, which leaves out a cracked sump's leak). Ranges 0..1 (Systems_Lubrication.xml, Systems_Cooling.xml).

checks.title: A fire put out within the hour leaves the coolant hot but under 120 C; one left to burn boils it over
checks.when: ofPlayer and count(samples(fire, 0, 1)) >= 20 and max(samples(fire, 0, 1)) > 0 and last(samples(fire, 0, 1)) == 0 and count(samples(coolant, -60, 200)) >= 20

note.variant: {'put out' if sum(samples(fire, 0, 1)) * 0.1 <= 1 else 'left to burn' if sum(samples(fire, 0, 1)) * 0.1 >= 2 else 'between'}

checks.why: Figures for row 29, from the saved graph histories (bodyFire's kept since Framework 0.346.0, the owner's yes of 27 Nov 2026). Fire heats the coolant 180 C an hour and the cab 80 at full size (Systems_Cooling.xml and Systems_Cabin.xml, fireHeat). Put out within the hour the coolant peaks near 102 C, under overheating's 120; two hours boils it over, 130 (FireFigureTests). fireHours is the saved day's fire weighted by its size, one sample a tenth of an hour: a full fire for an hour reads 1. Read once the fire is out (its last sample 0). Ranges: fire 0..1, coolant -60..200, cab -60..80.

checks.title: A parked truck's block heater holds its coolant far above the cold air
checks.when: ofPlayer and contains(fits, 'PhobosFitting_BlockHeater') and drafted != True and count(samples(coolant, -60, 200)) >= 40 and count(samples(cab, -60, 80)) >= 40 and max(tail(samples(cab, -60, 80), 40)) <= -5 and max(diffs(tail(samples(coolant, -60, 200), 40))) <= 1 and max(tail(samples(coolant, -60, 200), 40)) <= 45 and mean(tail(samples(coolant, -60, 200), 40)) - mean(tail(samples(cab, -60, 80), 40)) >= 10
checks.why: Figures for row 30. The block heater pulls the coolant toward engineHeaterTarget 40 C at engineHeaterRate 2 an hour, full below 35, against the soak's 0.6 toward the air (Systems_Cooling.xml), so it settles at (80 + 0.6 x air) / 2.6: about 28.5 C at -10 and 26 at -20. Read over the last four hours, parked on a map (a camp is a world object), engine off (not drafted, the coolant never rising a degree a sample), in a cab below -5 C, the cab standing for the air. Shore power is not saved, so a truck whose coolant is not 10 C above the cab is taken as unpowered and left out. Ranges: coolant -60..200, cab -60..80.

checks.title: With the drive belt gone and the engine running, the coolant climbs and the battery never charges
checks.when: ofPlayer and belt == 0 and drafted == True and count(samples(coolant, -60, 200)) >= 20 and count(samples(charge, 0, 1)) >= 20 and max(tail(samples(coolant, -60, 200), 20)) >= 60
checks.why: Figures for row 34. The belt turns the water pump and fan (the radiator flow reads the Belt role, Systems_Cooling.xml) and the alternator (charging's drivenByRole Belt, Systems_Electrical.xml), so with it destroyed the radiator does nothing and the battery takes no charge while the engine runs. Read over the last two hours of a vehicle whose engine is on at the save (Vehicle Framework's ignition/drafted) and warm. PhobosDriveBelt's 10 health is the default loadout's. Ranges: coolant -60..200, charge 0..1.

checks.title: An EMP that reaches the battery takes about 40% of its charge in one step, or 16% on a military vehicle
checks.when: ofPlayer and count(samples(charge, 0, 1)) >= 2 and min(diffs(samples(charge, 0, 1))) <= -0.08 and battery != None and battery >= 17
checks.why: Figures for row 92. An EMP that stuns the battery part costs it 2.5% of its health (Moderate, civilian) or 1% (Minor, military: armed), Vehicle Framework's EMPStunDamage with Rules_VehicleSystems.xml's empSeverityCivilian and empSeverityMilitary, and the battery loses 16 times that share of its charge (Systems_Electrical.xml, perShareLost -16): 0.40 or 0.16 in one step. A shot costs 0.01 a health point, so a drop of 0.08 with at most 3 of the battery's 20 health gone can only be an EMP. Armed is read from the saved turrets, as VehicleEmp.Rate decides it; a vehicle hardened by its upgrade tree reads civilian here. Range: charge 0..1.

checks.title: A Harrier with its avionics below 60% has its crew oxygen out, at the avionics part's efficiency
checks.when: ofPlayer and count(samples(oxygen, 0, 1)) >= 1 and avionics < 24 and last(samples(charge, 0, 1)) >= 0.05

figures.gap: round(last(samples(oxygen, 0, 1)) - (0 if avionics / 40 <= 0.25 else 0.4 * (avionics / 40 - 0.25) / 0.15 if avionics / 40 <= 0.4 else avionics / 40 if avionics / 40 <= 0.7 else 0.7 + 0.3 * (avionics / 40 - 0.7) / 0.15 if avionics / 40 <= 0.85 else 1), 3)

checks.why: Figures for row 144. crewOxygen is the oxygen parameter (1 on the Harrier) times the Avionics part's efficiency times the battery's curve (full from 5%) times the bleed (1 parked, or with every engine turning), Systems_Avionics.xml; below 0.6 it is out. The efficiency is Vehicle Framework's default curve (0 to 0.25 health nothing, 0.4 at 0.4, equal from 0.4 to 0.7, full from 0.85), so gap should be about 0. The avionics is D'thorga Patches' PhobosAvionics, the Harrier's part li[5] with 40 health (Parts_HarrierVtol.xml: the jet's four, the canopy, then the avionics), as of 27 Nov 2026. Range 0..1.

checks.title: A cab with its glass gone heats far faster in a fire than a sealed one
checks.when: ofPlayer and max(samples(fire, 0, 1)) > 0 and glass != None and drafted != True and count(samples(cab, -60, 80)) >= 20 and count(samples(coolant, -60, 200)) >= 20 and max(samples(cab, -60, 80)) >= 38 and max(diffs(samples(coolant, -60, 200))) >= 2
checks.why: Figures for row 396. A sealed cab takes 80 C an hour from a full fire against the insulation's pull of 2 toward the air; with the glass gone, fireThroughGlass adds eight times that and brokenGlass eight times the pull (Systems_Cabin.xml), the same heat about 40 C above the air nine times as fast. The cab's steepest six-minute rise is set against the coolant's, which the same fire heats at 180 an hour (Systems_Cooling.xml): about 0.4 at most sealed, about 1.8 with the glass gone. Engine off, so the engine's heat does not swell the coolant's steps. The glass is read at the save: a fire wears it 0.6 of its health an hour (FireWear.xml), so a sealed cab left burning near two hours reads gone. Ranges: cab -60..80, coolant -60..200. The fire is read from its own saved history (Framework 0.346.0).
